## Who is Jared Kushner?

Son of prominent real estate developer Charles Kushner, Jared Corey Kushner was born on January 10th 1981 in New Jersey. Both Kushners have had extensive ties to the Trump administration;

Charles Kushner was pardoned by Trump in 2020, and in 2025 he became a US ambassador to France. Kushner was made to serve two years in jail for his later pardoned charges, which included tax evasion and witness tampering.

Jared Kushner has been married to Trump’s daughter, Ivanka, since 2009.

Kushner is one of the president’s closest confidants, having been his senior advisor during his first term and being a Special Envoy for Peace during Trump’s current term.

His history in business.

Jared’s father, Charles founded the family real estate business Kushner Companies in 1985. Jared temporarily took over the business in 2005 when Charles was sent to prison.

Kushner Companies’ primary influence is in New Jersey’s residential markets. Their website states that: “Kushner is a generational owner, developer, builder, and operator of high-quality real estate with a primary focus on multifamily.”

Kushner’s most notable business venture is his private investment firm, Affinity Partners. Established by Kushner after Trump’s first term in 2021, Affinity Partners has become a topic of debate following Kushner’s return to the Trump Administration and his introduction to international politics.

Affinity and the Middle East.

Since its establishment, Affinity has raised around $6 billion, with the majority of the company’s funding coming from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates.

Saudi Arabia’s Sovereign Wealth Fund was the first and is the largest investment made to Affinity. With this, the country is given the first opportunity to invest when Affinity tries to raise more money.

Chimera Investments, a Dubai-based private investment firm, is also a main funder. The firm is a part of the Dubai business empire, which is overseen by the UAE’s national security advisor.

Kushner and the Middle East.

On February 19th, Kushner was appointed as a Special Envoy for Peace by President Trump. Kushner would join fellow investor Steve Witkoff to help broker peace deals with other countries.

His first introduction to geopolitics was the 2020 Abraham Accords, for which he was nominated for a Nobel Peace Prize for his involvement.

The accords established diplomatic ties between many different Gulf countries and Israel, essentially a ‘peace deal.’

Cause for concern.

Kushner was appointed to be a Special Envoy for Peace without Senate approval.

Additionally, presidential appointees and US security agents are required to file public financial statements for public disclosure. They are also required to undergo a “life history” examination to “ensure that applicants: [a]re free from conflicting allegiances ... [a]re not a potential risk for blackmail ... and [w]ill abide by regulations.”

Technically, the US Office of Personnel Management can excuse an appointment of less than 30 days (under the pretense of a nationwide threat).

Former Ethics Czar Norm Eisen has accused both Trump and Kushner of violating multiple ethics-related statutes and laws with Kushner’s Special Envoy appointment.

Anti-Nepotism Statute: Kushner is Trump’s son-in-law, and according to this statute, no individual may be appointed to any government position if a person who is either serving or exerting control over the agency publicly advocates for the individual.

18 USC. § 208: No government employee is allowed to participate, either personally or substantially, in government matters that influence their own personal financial interests. Affinity’s biggest investor is Saudi Arabia, a longtime rival of Iran. The firm receives millions of dollars in management fees from the Saudi Arabian government each year. Kushner also led peace discussions with Iran and is a key architect of the “New Gaza” plan, leading to Eisen calling for Kushner to be removed from his position.
